analysis.investment_thesis: Active Infrastructures is a genuine micro-cap (267 Cr) with strong promoter skin-in-the-game (72.38%) and an impressive revenue ramp from 1 Cr to 90 Cr, but civil construction is a commoditized, working-capital-heavy business where scaling nationally is difficult. At P/E 26x with margins still thin and FY25 revenue de-growing vs FY24, the valuation doesn't offer the margin of safety I demand for small-cap entry.
key_strengths: Micro-cap (267 Cr) with promoter holding 72.38% — strong skin in the game
Equity raised from 27 Cr to 116 Cr in FY25 (IPO capital), borrowings down 109→60 Cr — deleveraging
EBITDA margin expanding: 15% (FY23) → 31% (FY25); ROCE healthy at 15.5%
key_risks: Revenue dipped in FY25 (97→90 Cr) — growth not linear; construction is lumpy/order-book dependent
P/E 26x on a 13 Cr PAT base is rich for a civil contractor — no value entry
FY25 OCF collapsed to 5 Cr vs 32 Cr in FY24 — working capital stress typical of EPC
red_flags: FCF declining (11→5→2 Cr) despite revenue scale — cash conversion weak
analysis.detailed_analysis: From the SMILE lens, this ticks Small (267 Cr cap), Medium experience (incorporated 2007), and promoter-aligned (72.38%). The transformation from 1 Cr revenue in FY22 to 90 Cr in FY25 with margin expansion (EBITDA 15%→31%) and post-IPO deleveraging (borrowings 109→60 Cr, equity 27→116 Cr) is genuinely interesting — classic inflection-point profile. Infra/construction TAM in India is large, but penetration is not the issue; fragmentation and competitive bidding are.\n\nWhat holds me back: FY25 revenue actually fell from 97 to 90 Cr, FCF has degraded to 2 Cr, and at P/E 26x on a 13 Cr profit base, the market has already priced in optimism. Civil contractors rarely compound as multibaggers because receivables balloon with growth and margins mean-revert. I'd want to see two more years of order-book execution, sustained 20%+ revenue growth, and P/E compression to 12-15x before committing. Watchlist, not buy.
